challenges.text: Eli Moreno: 65% productive time assumes that travel, keys and tool collection are coordinated. Our September diary put those losses at 43% of offered time. Keep separate time entries for repairs, retrofit, travel and access; review after two months before claiming that pooling works.

Sana Patel: the 16 extra hours come from four people, not all 120 households. Two are carers. Publish the rota two weeks ahead, accept withdrawals without penalty, and compare an eight-hour month. Repair priority must not depend on volunteering.

Theo Grant: 80 material units are a model index, not £80 or 80 kits. Supplier quote AQ-26-104 covers 24 homes at £6,240 plus £960 contingency; it excludes roof membranes and two heating valves. Do not convert the model total into a purchase order.

Leila Okafor: 40% fewer new repair units is unsupported. Seals and fans may reduce damp but cannot fix roof drainage, boilers or old pipe joints. Use 20% for the next comparison; keep incoming problems by category and compare a full winter before claiming an effect.

Jon Bell: the four-month schedule reserves 48 productive hours each month and leaves only 1.8 repair units of capacity. With 36 unresolved units in the November register, that allocation is untenable. Spread the same 192 retrofit hours over six months and protect urgent visits first.

Maya Chen: one repair unit can be a fan replacement or a recurring leak; neither is one household. January's 37 unresolved units affect 29 homes. The model treats them as equal eight-hour jobs and averages monthly arrivals. Show both counts in the review and keep urgent hazards out of the ordinary queue.

Eli Moreno: 168 of 192 retrofit hours are logged by February, but the December and January repair diary includes specialist hours outside the modeled pool. Those hours do not prove the cooperative can sustain 65% productivity. Audit the extra contractor time before approving another building.
QA: audit the specialist hours before adding another block.

decisions.action: Run one shared repair rota across Riverside, Parkside and Hilltop for October. Eli holds the tool cupboard keys; each resident steward confirms access before Thursday's work list is published. Reserve the existing 80 offered hours plus up to 16 opt-in hours; do not book retrofit work yet.
decisions.rationale: There are 30 unresolved repair units across 120 homes. Separate crews lose time collecting tools and arranging access. The shared-rota scenario predicts 26.7 unresolved units after one month and 10.2 after six; these are workload estimates, not promises to residents. Test the coordination change before buying materials.
decisions.authority: Alder maintenance committee, minutes AM-2026-09-18, approved a one-month rota trial within the existing repair budget. Maya Chen can coordinate access; Eli can assign agreed work. Neither can enter a home or expand the pilot without permission.
decisions.consent: Resident consent is recorded separately for every visit. Four contributors offered up to four hours each for October; they may withdraw. Leila, Jon and Sana check that non-volunteers receive the same repair priority. No access agreement is inferred from cooperative membership.
decisions.success: Close at least six repair units in October; publish the unresolved count by area; log offered, productive and access-loss hours separately. Every urgent report receives a same-day triage call and an agreed safety response before routine work.
decisions.reversal: End the pooled rota if a resident loses repair access, if a volunteer is pressured to continue, or if fewer than six units close without an explained access delay. Return keys and outstanding jobs to the area stewards; retain every repair commitment.

decisions.action: Keep the shared rota and invite eight homes in each area to a ventilation-and-seal retrofit pilot. Cap the initial materials order at £6,240, with £960 held as contingency. Eli checks fan routes and moisture sources before any installation; Maya records individual opt-ins.
decisions.rationale: October closed seven repair units and added five, leaving 28 unresolved. Residents asked for fewer repeat damp visits. The four-month scenario reserves 48 productive hours a month for retrofit and predicts 40.8 unresolved units at its peak, then 0 at month 12. We are accepting a temporary backlog increase to test recurrence reduction; the 40% assumption remains disputed.
decisions.authority: Maintenance committee minutes AM-2026-10-15 authorize a 24-home invitation and the initial purchase cap. Theo releases funds only against the itemized quote; any roof or boiler work goes through the separate repair budget. A district-wide retrofit has not been authorized.
decisions.consent: A home joins only after a resident reviews the work, access window and withdrawal route. Twenty of the 24 invited homes opted in; four deferred. No installation occurs in a deferred home. Workers agree task scope, safety arrangements and compensation before booking.
decisions.success: Complete the access survey in all 20 consenting homes; publish a parts list and actual retrofit hours. Keep urgent repair access intact. Bring a four- versus six-month comparison and the challenged 20% reduction assumption to the November review before releasing the next batch.
decisions.reversal: Pause the next batch if unresolved units exceed 35, a survey finds a moisture source that sealing could worsen, or an urgent visit is delayed by retrofit work. Unspent contingency remains held. Completed safe installations stay in place; assess removal individually if harm is reported.

decisions.action: Replace the four-month comparison with a six-month schedule and a 20% recurrence assumption. Cap planned retrofit effort at 32 productive hours a month, with urgent repairs taking precedence. Continue only the 20 opted-in homes; route roof leaks and heating valves to specialist repair work.
decisions.rationale: November added ten repair units and closed two, leaving 36; the previous pause threshold was crossed and the next batch was held. A six-month comparison leaves 34.2 unresolved units at month 6 and 9 at month 12, versus 30.6 and 0 for the original four-month comparison. The slower schedule releases more repair capacity now and claims less benefit later. Neither forecast models the actual sequence of our changes.
decisions.steward: Eli Moreno · maintenance lead; Maya Chen · access coordinator
decisions.authority: Maintenance committee minutes AM-2026-11-18 release the held batch under the revised hour cap. Theo retains the £960 contingency; the committee must approve any increase. Area stewards can stop an individual visit when access or safety conditions are unmet.
decisions.consent: Reconfirm scope with the same 20 households after the schedule change. Leila, Jon and Sana offer separate access slots; no household has to accept a shared appointment. Volunteers confirm each monthly rota; declining hours does not change a household's repair position.
decisions.success: Finish the 192-hour modeled retrofit scope without expanding the consent group. Report remaining repair units and affected homes separately each month. Keep all urgent visits within their agreed response window; compare recurring damp reports only after the scope is complete and winter conditions are recorded.
decisions.reversal: Stop new installations if unresolved units exceed 40 at a reconciled month-end, if two urgent visits miss their agreed safety response, or if a retrofit worsens moisture or ventilation. Move available cooperative hours to repairs; retain the opt-out route and commission an independent inspection of any affected installation.

decisions.action: Finish the existing retrofit scope; authorize no additional homes. Eli closes the final inspection list and gives repairs the next unallocated slot. Theo reconciles contractor hours and materials. Bring the March backlog count, household count and recurrence log to the committee before considering expansion.
decisions.rationale: February has 39 unresolved units versus 33.5 in the six-month comparison. The diary records 168 retrofit hours and 16 inspected homes; four inspections remain. The 20% reduction is still an assumption, with benefits only modeled from month 7. Finish and inspect the small pilot while protecting repairs; evidence does not support expanding it.
decisions.steward: Maya Chen · review owner; Theo Grant · reconciliation
decisions.authority: Maintenance committee minutes AM-2027-02-16 approve completion of the existing scope only. Theo can pay accepted invoices within the original £7,200 envelope. Expansion, an increased budget or new household invitations require a fresh committee decision and individual consent.
decisions.consent: All 20 participants receive an inspection appointment and a plain record of installed work; four deferred homes remain outside the pilot. No resident is required to provide indoor sensor data. Recurrence reports are collected through stewards with household identifiers withheld from the shared export.
decisions.success: Reconcile all 192 retrofit hours, inspect all 20 participating homes and document any outstanding defects. Publish the six-month stock balance and all specialist hours. Do not claim a 20% improvement from a single month; agree a full-winter comparison and a follow-up inspection before requesting expansion.
decisions.reversal: Keep expansion paused while the audited backlog is 40 or higher. If it exceeds 40, redirect the next available cooperative hours to repairs and request a specialist capacity review. Any installation-related harm pauses that installation type immediately; offer assessment and remedial work without requiring continued participation.

observations.note: Leila Okafor · preliminary October count. Six closures are verified and five new issues have arrived: 30 + 5 − 6 = 29. A seventh fan replacement awaits resident confirmation. Four Riverside visits moved when access slots changed; the rota records the lost time rather than treating those homes as refusals.

Theo Grant · reconciled October register. The resident confirmed the seventh closure: 30 + 5 − 7 = 28, across 23 homes. Riverside 12, Parkside 9, Hilltop 7. The shared-rota comparison predicts 26.7; the 1.3-unit gap reflects access delays and one more arrival than its 4.5-unit monthly average. This supersedes the provisional count of 29 without deleting it.

Jon Bell · preliminary November count. Ten arrivals followed the cold spell, including six pipe-joint or roof-drainage leaks outside the retrofit scope. Only one repair closure is verified: 28 + 10 − 1 = 37. The second heating-valve repair is awaiting its pressure-test record. Hold the next retrofit batch because the decision's 35-unit threshold has been crossed.

Eli Moreno · reconciled November register. Both closures now have resident confirmation and test records: 28 + 10 − 2 = 36, across 28 homes. Riverside 15, Parkside 12, Hilltop 9. This exceeds the four-month comparison's 35.4 and triggers its pause condition. The six-month alternative is a new September-baseline comparison, not a forecast stitched to the actual October rota.

Sana Patel · reconciled December register. Five new units and six closures: 36 + 5 − 6 = 35, across 27 homes. Riverside 14, Parkside 12, Hilltop 9. Two closures used separately funded specialist time. All urgent reports received the agreed safety response; do not treat contractor-supported throughput as proof of the pooled-hours assumption. Retrofit log: 104 hours to date.

Leila Okafor · preliminary January register. Six arrivals and three verified closures: 35 + 6 − 3 = 38. A Riverside condensation job was marked complete after sealing, but the resident reports a wet sill after rain. Keep it open pending a source check; do not count an installation as a successful repair.

Theo Grant · reconciled January register. A separate Parkside fan replacement is confirmed; the wet-sill job stays open. Six arrivals and four closures: 35 + 6 − 4 = 37, across 29 homes. Riverside 15, Parkside 13, Hilltop 9. The selected comparison predicts 32.8. Retrofit work totals 136 hours; the inspection log distinguishes completed work from accepted installations.

Maya Chen · reconciled February register. Six arrivals and four closures: 37 + 6 − 4 = 39, across 31 homes. Riverside 16, Parkside 13, Hilltop 10. Retrofit work totals 168 hours and 16 of 20 homes have final inspection records. No urgent response window was missed. The backlog is 5.5 above the 33.5-unit comparison; expansion remains on hold.

Jon Bell · preliminary March register. Five arrivals are recorded and two closures are verified: 39 + 5 − 2 = 42. Two other completed jobs await resident confirmation. Eli has moved the next unallocated work slot to repairs while the count is reconciled; no additional retrofit invitation or order has been issued.

Theo Grant · reconciled March register. Four closures are confirmed: 39 + 5 − 4 = 40, across 32 homes. Riverside 17, Parkside 13, Hilltop 10. From September: 30 starting units + 37 new − 27 closed = 40. Retrofit work totals 192 hours and all 20 opted-in homes are inspected. The selected fixed-baseline comparison predicts 34.2, a 5.8-unit gap. Expansion stays paused at the decision's 40-unit boundary; there is no measured 20% recurrence reduction yet.
QA follow-up: two late reports await triage.
